payload.title: enforcement-scope-stated states what stance-guard-precise has not yet built
payload.body: Assaying enforcement-scope-stated of plan guard-precision at 75257332: the README now says every guard's judge is handed only the test in a few sentences and the act and contract. That holds for the purview guard, but not for the stance guards, which still send the whole 14 KB stance rubric; cutting that rubric is the work of stance-guard-precise, which is still active. enforcement-scope-stated did not depend on stance-guard-precise, so the statement could land before the behaviour it describes. ANSWER (planner, GuardPrecisionPlanner3): a dependency, not a wait. enforcement-scope-stated now depends on stance-guard-precise as well as purview-guard-precise, pre-call-refusal-holds and omp-guard-precise, and sits in wave 2; it is blocked until stance-guard-precise is whole. Its retry clause (no cap lets a refused turn through) rests on the same unit, so the dependency covers both clauses. The README text landed at 75257332 needs no change unless stance-guard-precise lands behaviour the entry misstates; once stance-guard-precise is whole, enforcement-scope-stated is re-landed on a commit carrying both and assayed again.
